sections.h2: How to compare providers in different regions
sections.html:
A provider's location affects more than price. Before you shortlist, check these points for each country you are considering:

  • Credentials and registration: professional titles and registers differ by country, so ask for the exact body and a registration number you can look up yourself. Each service page lists typical credentials by country.
  • Contract and governing law: know which country's law applies, where disputes would be heard and in which language the contract is binding.
  • Currency and invoicing: agree the currency, who bears exchange-rate movement, and whether tax is added to quotes.
  • Time zones: overlap of even two or three working hours makes reviews and urgent fixes much easier.
  • Data handling: if the work involves personal data, see our guide to GDPR when outsourcing.
  • Local knowledge: for tax, payroll, legal and compliance work, local rules matter more than a lower day rate.

Regulated work such as tax filings, payroll and legal advice generally benefits from a provider who works in the relevant country every day. Creative and technical work, such as web design, software development or copywriting, is easier to source globally. Many businesses combine the two: a local accountant for filings plus a remote team for delivery. Use the project brief builder to describe the job once and send it to providers in several regions to compare like for like.

faqs.q: Do I need a provider in the same country as my business?
faqs.a: Not for every service. Regulated work like tax and payroll usually needs local expertise, while design, development and marketing can often be delivered remotely.

faqs.q: How do I compare quotes from different countries?
faqs.a: Ask each provider to quote in the same currency for the same written brief, and confirm whether tax, expenses and revisions are included.

faqs.q: How do I check a foreign provider's credentials?
faqs.a: Ask for the professional body and registration number, then search that body's public register yourself rather than relying on a certificate sent by the provider.
